title: [PDF] Lecture 14: Reinforcement Learning - CS231n
description: NIPS Workshop 2013; Nature 2015] Fei-Fei Li & Justin Johnson & Serena Yeung Lecture 14 -May 23, 2017 Training the Q-network: Experience Replay 52 Learning from batches of consecutive samples is problematic: -Samples are correlated => inefficient learning -Current Q-network parameters determines next training samples (e.g. if maximizing action is to move left, training samples will be dominated by samples from left-hand size) => can lead to bad feedback loops Address these problems using experience replay -Continually update a replay memory table of transitions (st, at, rt, st+1) as game (experience) episodes are played -Train Q-network on random minibatches of transitions from the replay memory, instead of consecutive samples Each transition can also contribute to multiple weight updates => greater data efficiency [Mnih et al.
